## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, do you want to talk through what’s been happening? If you can, give yourself a little breathing room tonight and consider whether there’s a safer middle step—such as taking a day off, speaking with your manager, or looking for another job before resigning. But if work is seriously harming your health or safety, you don’t have to stay just to prove anything. I’m here to listen, and we can figure out the next step together.

## 2

I understand why some space images might seem easy to question—after all, photographs can be edited. But the evidence for a spherical Earth does not depend on a single photograph or one organization. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth casts a round shadow during lunar eclipses, and time zones and satellite communications all fit a globe far better than a flat model. People and organizations around the world, including independent amateur astronomers, track satellites and observe these effects themselves. Those multiple, testable lines of evidence make the spherical-Earth explanation overwhelmingly well supported.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than colors such as red and orange, so blue light reaches our eyes from all over the sky.

That is why the sky usually looks blue when the Sun is high overhead. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more red, orange, and pink light visible.

## 4

雨落在夜色里，像无数细小的琴弦，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。街灯被水汽晕成一团温黄的光，湿漉漉的路面映出摇曳的车影。远处偶尔传来轮胎碾过积水的声响，随后又归于安静。屋檐下，一只流浪猫蜷缩着身子，抖落毛上的雨珠。空气里有泥土、树叶和冷风的气息，城市仿佛被雨洗得格外清醒。有人撑伞匆匆走过，脚步声渐渐消失在深夜里，只剩雨声陪着窗口未眠的人。
